source_units.text_en: This Document
This document is a TOGAF® Series Guide to Business Scenarios. It has been developed and approved by The Open Group.

Business Scenarios provide a mechanism to fully understand the requirements of information technology and align it with business needs. This is accomplished through the analysis of business processes, supporting IT components, and information flow requirements. Business Scenarios are an essential tool used by the successful manager to achieve Boundaryless Information Flow™.
The document supersedes G261: Manager’s Guide to Business Scenarios.
More information is available, along with a number of tools, guides, and other resources, at www.opengroup.org/architecture.

sections.translation_zh:
TOGAF® 系列指南说明如何使用 TOGAF 标准，以及如何裁剪以满足具体需要。

系列指南预期是 TOGAF 标准中发展最快的部分，定位为标准的指导部分。TOGAF 基础内容预期保持长期稳定，而使用指导可针对行业、架构风格、用途与问题。例如，扩展企业转型所需的利益相关者、关注点、视图与支撑模型，可能与内部 IT 环境迁移到云所需内容显著不同；两者都使用 ADM，都从架构愿景开始，开发目标架构，并走向实施与迁移计划。TOGAF 基础内容是跨行业、领域和风格的必要支架。

source_units.text_en: About the TOGAF® Series Guides
The TOGAF® Series Guides contain guidance on how to use the TOGAF Standard and how to adapt it to fulfill specific needs.

The TOGAF® Series Guides are expected to be the most rapidly developing part of the TOGAF Standard and are positioned as the guidance part of the standard. While the TOGAF Fundamental Content is expected to be long-lived and stable, guidance on the use of the TOGAF Standard can be industry, architectural style, purpose, and problem-specific. For example, the stakeholders, concerns, views, and supporting models required to support the transformation of an extended enterprise may be significantly different than those used to support the transition of an in-house IT environment to the cloud; both will use the Architecture Development Method (ADM), start with an Architecture Vision, and develop a Target Architecture on the way to an Implementation and Migration Plan. The TOGAF Fundamental Content remains the essential scaffolding across industry, domain, and style.

企业架构成功的一个关键因素，是它与业务需求的关联程度，以及它能否可证明地支持并使能企业实现业务目标。任何架构工作都必须从“解决方案需要满足的需求”的基线视图开始。试想在不了解“为何需要仓库”的情况下指导建造仓库：可能建成一座适合存放大型机械部件的优秀仓库，但实际需求是存放家庭用品。在不理解“为什么”的情况下创建架构，通常会导致解决方案与需求错配。

**业务场景方法**是一种通过理解并记录业务场景关键要素、在连续迭代中验证、细化或改变架构工作前提的技术。其中：

- 每次迭代都需要规划、数据收集、分析、文档化与评审；
- 每次迭代应改进一个或多个关键要素；
- 迭代重复进行，直到理解程度足以支持“继续推进”的决策。

不审视业务场景的全部要素，存在产出不完整解决方案的风险；但也必须注意避免不必要的反复。

业务场景方法可用于企业架构开发的多个阶段——主要是预备阶段、架构愿景与业务架构阶段，必要时也可用于其他架构阶段——以直接从业务高层需求推导架构特征。该技术用于帮助识别、理解并记录业务需求，从而导出架构开发必须处理的业务需求，并以**业务场景**文档记录。

业务场景是对以下内容的统一描述：

- 真实业务问题；
- 问题发生的业务与技术环境；
- 由业务能力 [G211] 使能的价值流 [G178]；
- 正确执行后的期望成果；
- 提供这些能力的人与计算组件（“参与者”）。


良好的业务场景还应是“SMART”的：

- **具体**（Specific）：明确业务中需要做什么；
- **可度量**（Measurable）：通过清晰的成功度量指标；
- **可行动**（Actionable）：清晰切分问题，并为确定解决方案要素与计划提供基础；
- **现实**（Realistic）：问题可在物理现实、时间与成本约束内解决；
- **有时限**（Time-bound）：明确说明解决方案机会何时失效。

第 9 章给出应考虑成果的详细示例。无论采用何种成果，关键都是使其 SMART。

关于业务场景与业务场景方法的进一步说明：

- **业务场景不只关乎 IT**，尽管其起源如此。业务场景同样关乎理解业务价值、价值流与业务成果，以及改进价值流、达成成果、交付业务价值通常需要哪些资源。
- **业务场景不限于 IT 行业**，该技术可应用于医疗、交通、油气、彩票等任何行业的需求理解。
- **业务场景不只适用于大问题领域**，既可应用于国家彩票标准等非常广泛的问题，也可应用于零售 POS 升级等非常聚焦的小问题。
- **业务场景与架构一样不是终点**——终点是达成期望的业务成果。因此，必须有下游路径用业务场景驱动架构工作，并忠实驱动解决方案实施。
- **业务场景是特定时点的陈述**，应随重大变化更新。

业务场景**不是**：

- 用例（如 OMG、Rational 软件中的用例）——用例是更详细的人与计算机交互描述，通常用于软件开发项目；
- 业务模型、商业论证或业务场景计划——但业务场景可由公司业务模型启发，SMART 业务场景也可为商业论证/业务模型/计划提供输入；
- SPIN（情境、问题、暗示、需求满足的销售策略）——SPIN 是可用于为业务场景收集信息的销售技术，业务场景可为 SPIN 提供相关语境；
- 任何典型工程规格（如 IEEE 规格）的替代品——后者更详细、更面向材料，并更贴近科学。

source_units.text_en: 1. Introduction

A key factor in the success of an Enterprise Architecture is the extent to which it is linked to business requirements, and demonstrably supporting and enabling the enterprise to achieve its business objectives. Any architectural effort must begin with a baseline view of the needs to be fulfilled by the solution or solutions. Consider guiding the construction of a warehouse building without understanding why the warehouse is needed. This could result in a fine warehouse solution for housing large-scale mechanical parts; however, the need was a warehouse for household goods. Creating an architecture without understanding “why” typically results in mismatches between solutions and needs.

The Business Scenario method is a technique to validate, elaborate, and/or change the premise behind an architecture effort by understanding and documenting the key elements of a Business Scenario in successive iterations where:
• Each iteration requires planning, data gathering, analysis, documentation, and review
• Each iteration should improve one or more of the key elements
• Iterations are repeated until your understanding is fit-for-purpose for deciding to move forward
Not examining all elements of a Business Scenario carries a risk of producing an incomplete solution, but care must be taken not to iterate unnecessarily.

The Business Scenario method may be used at various stages of developing an Enterprise Architecture – principally the Preliminary, Architecture Vision, and Business Architecture phases – but in other architecting phases as well, if required, to derive the characteristics of the architecture directly from the high-level requirements of the business. The technique is used to help identify, understand, and document business needs, and thereby to derive the business requirements that the architecture development has to address. These business requirements are documented as a Business Scenario.
A Business Scenario is a uniform description of:
• Real business problems
• The business and technology environment in which those problems occur
• Value streams [G178] enabled by capabilities [G211]
• The desired outcome(s) of proper execution
• The human and computing components (the “actors”) who provide the capabilities
A good Business Scenario is also “SMART”:
• Specific, by defining what needs to be done in the business
• Measurable, through clear metrics for success
• Actionable, by:
◦Clearly segmenting the problem
◦Providing the basis for determining elements and plans for the solution
• Realistic, in that the problem can be solved within the bounds of physical reality, time, and cost constraints
• Time-bound, in that there is a clear statement of when the solution opportunity expires
Chapter 9 provides detailed examples of outcomes that should be considered. Whatever outcomes are used, the idea is to make those outcomes SMART.
Below are further notes on Business Scenarios and the Business Scenario method:
• Business Scenarios are not just about IT, even though that was their genesis

Business Scenarios are just as much about understanding business value, value streams, and business outcomes and what resources in general are required to improve the value streams and meet outcomes to deliver business value.

• Business Scenarios are not specific to the IT industry, rather the technique can be applied to help understand the requirements in any industry such as Healthcare, Transportation, Oil and Gas, Lottery, etc.

• Business Scenarios are not just relevant to big problem areas; the technique can be applied to very large general problems areas such as standards for National Lotteries, or very small focused problem areas such as retail Point of Sale upgrades
• Business Scenarios, just like architectures, are not the end game – the end game is achieving the desired business outcomes
Thus, there must be a downstream path for using the Business Scenario to drive the architecture work which must faithfully drive implementation of solutions.
• Business Scenarios are statements at a specific time and should be updated to reflect significant changes
Business Scenarios are not:
• Use-cases (as in OMG®, Rational SW, …); use-cases are:
◦More detailed descriptions of human to computer interaction
◦Typically used in software development projects
• Business models nor business cases nor Business Scenario plans (as in Forbes …):
◦However, a Business Scenario can be informed by a company’s business model
◦A SMART Business Scenario can inform a business case and/or a business model and/or
Business Scenario plan
• SPIN (as in Situation, Problem, Implication, Need Payoff selling strategy):
◦SPIN is a sales technique that can be used to gather information for a Business Scenario
◦A Business Scenario can provide the seller some relevant “context” for a SPIN engagement
• A substitute for any typical engineering specifications (as from IEEE®):
◦Which are much more detailed, material-specific, and tied more to science

sections.translation_zh:
业务场景本质上是对业务问题的完整描述——既从业务角度、也从架构角度——使各项需求能够在整体问题的语境中相互关联地审视。缺少这样的完整描述作为语境：

- 架构有基于不完整需求集的风险，这些需求不能构成完整的问题描述，从而误导架构工作；
- 解决问题的业务价值不清晰；
- 潜在解决方案的相关性不清晰。

此外，由于该技术要求业务线管理者与其他利益相关者在架构项目早期参与，它在赢得这些关键人员对项目及最终产物（企业架构）的认同方面也发挥重要作用。

业务场景的另一个优势是**与供应商沟通**。当今多数架构通过最大限度利用商用现成品（COTS）软件实现，这些软件常来自多个供应商并在公开市场采购。客户使用业务场景可帮助供应商交付恰当解决方案：供应商需确保其解决方案组件为开放解决方案增值并具有市场性；业务场景提供了供应商社区把客户问题与解决方案联系起来的语言。它不仅说明需要什么、为什么需要，还使供应商能够利用开放标准、借助彼此技能来最优地解决问题。

创建业务场景需要时间与精力；若做得对，这项投资会有回报，回报汇总如下。若不开展，或做得不对，解决方案开发人员与实际业务之间将持续存在更多同类问题：

- **更好的解决方案**：通过理解真实需求及解决这些需求对业务的价值，可带来与业务清晰对齐、并实现新能力的解决方案。与业务领导者会面并把更好的解决方案摆上桌面，可形成可重复的关系，带来引入新能力的良性循环。
- **更快实现能力**：通过理解真实需求及相关时间要求，解决方案可按时间序列交付，而非一次性“大爆炸”式交付，从而更快实现与业务需求对齐的增量价值，这也与敏捷和 DevOps 方法一致。
- **更低成本**：通过理解真实业务需求并增量处理，最终节省成本——既节约成本，也避免成本。节约成本的例子包括只实现所需内容、消除冗余；避免成本的例子包括消除失败实施的代价、降低集成与互操作成本。

source_units.text_en: 2. Benefits of Business Scenarios

A Business Scenario is essentially a complete description of a business problem, both in business and in architectural terms, which enables individual requirements to be viewed in relation to one another in the context of the overall problem. Without such a complete description to serve as context:
• There is a danger of the architecture being based on an incomplete set of requirements that do not add up to a whole problem description, and that can therefore misguide architecture work
• The business value of solving the problem is unclear
• The relevance of potential solutions is unclear

Also, because the technique requires the involvement of business line management and other stakeholders at an early stage in the architecture project, it also plays an important role in gaining the buy-in of these key personnel to the overall project and its end-product – the Enterprise Architecture.

An additional advantage of Business Scenarios is in communication with vendors. Most architecture today is implemented by making maximum use of Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software solutions, often from multiple vendors, procured in the open market. The use of Business Scenarios by a customer can be an important aid to vendors in delivering appropriate solutions. Vendors need to ensure that their solution components add value to an open solution and are marketable. Business Scenarios provide a language with which the vendor community can link customer problems and solutions. Besides making obvious what is needed, and why, they allow vendors to solve problems optimally, using open standards and leveraging each other’s skills.

Creating a Business Scenario takes time and effort and if done right there is a return on this investment summarized in the following list. If not done, or done wrong, more of the same issues will exist between solutions developers and the actual business.

• Better solutions – by understanding the real needs and how solving these needs are valued by the business, solutions can be brought to bear that are clearly aligned to the business and enable new capabilities
By meeting with the leaders of the business and bringing better solutions to the table, a relationship develops that is repeatable, resulting in a virtuous cycle of bringing in new capabilities.

• Faster to realize capabilities – by understanding the real needs, and the timeline requirements associated with fulfillment of those needs, solutions can be brought to bear in a timed sequence rather than in a single big-bang approach
This results in faster implementations of incremental value aligned to business needs. This is also consistent with Agile and DevOps approaches to solving problems.
• Cheaper costs – by understanding real business needs and addressing them incrementally the ultimate savings are in costs – both costs saved and costs avoided

Examples of costs saved are implementing only what is needed and eliminating redundancy. Examples of costs avoided are eliminating the costs of failed implementations and lowering the costs of integration and interoperation.

sections.translation_zh:
创建业务场景包括完成六个步骤，覆盖图 3-1 的五个要素：

1. 识别、记录并排序驱动该场景的问题；
2. 识别场景的业务与技术环境，并在场景模型（含价值流与业务能力）中记录；
3. 识别并记录期望成果（成功处理问题的结果），使其 SMART；
4. 识别人的参与者及其在业务模型中的位置；
5. 识别计算机参与者（计算元素）及其在技术模型中的位置；
6. 检验“适用性”，仅在必要时细化。

图 3-1：创建业务场景。原图、图元及当前关系解释读取本节 structured_references。

关键术语说明：

- **成果**：项目或组织所提供之物带来的变化、收益、学习或其他效果。
- **能力**：组织、人或系统拥有的本领。开发业务场景时，指在已知环境中通过价值流中的人力/物力资源达成成果的能力。
- **业务能力**：企业为达成特定目的或成果而可能拥有或交换的特定能力或才能 [G211]。
- **价值流**：为客户、利益相关者或最终用户创造整体结果的端到端增值活动集合的表示 [G178]。开发业务场景时，指特定行业企业为市场交付有价值产品或服务而执行的一组活动。
- **价值主张**：对客户购买并使用你的产品和/或服务将获得的具体结果的清晰陈述，聚焦成果，以客户易于理解和记住的简明方式表达，并应缓解其痛点。业务场景并不显式记录价值主张，但对解决方案提供方而言，理解客户业务场景的重要性怎么强调都不为过。

业务场景通过若干阶段开发，以形成、验证并细化驱动架构工作的业务需求前提。每个阶段由规划、收集信息、分析信息、记录结果与评审结果等步骤组成（图 3-2）。每个阶段中，业务场景各要素依次改进；细化阶段决定是认为场景已完成并进入 TOGAF ADM 下一阶段，还是需要进一步细化——判断标准是“当前业务场景是否适合把需求传递到架构过程下游”。

图 3-2：开发业务场景的阶段与步骤。原图、图元与当前关系解释读取本节 structured_references。

这三个业务场景开发阶段及其步骤详见图 3-2 和第 3.2 节。

> 编者说明：这里同时存在三个不同层次：识别场景五要素的六个工作事项、每阶段重复的五个步骤，以及前提形成/初步验证/细化三个开发阶段。它们不能合并成一条十几个节点的唯一强制顺序。

source_units.text_en: 3.1. The Overall Process
Creating a Business Scenario involves completing the six steps that capture the five elements illustrated in Figure 3-1:
1. Identifying, documenting, and ranking the problem driving the scenario
2. Identifying the business and technical environment of the scenario and documenting it in scenario models including value streams and business capabilities
3. Identifying and documenting desired outcomes (the results of handling the problems successfully); get “SMART”
4. Identifying the human actors (participants) and their place in the business model
5. Identifying computer actors (computing elements) and their place in the technology model
6. Checking for “fitness-for-purpose” and refining only if necessary
Figure 3-1: Creating a Business Scenario
Below are explanations of a few key terms:
• Outcomes are the changes, benefits, learning, or other effects that happen as a result of what the project or organization offers or provides
• A capability is an ability that an organization, person, or system possesses
When developing a Business Scenario, this means the ability to achieve an outcome within a known environment through application of human and/or material resources in a value stream.
• A business capability is a particular ability or capacity that a business may possess or exchange to achieve a specific purpose or outcome [G211]
• A value stream is a representation of an end-to-end collection of value-adding activities that create an overall result for a customer, stakeholder, or end user [G178]
When developing a Business Scenario, this is a set of activities that a firm operating in a specific industry performs in order to deliver a valuable product or service for the market.

• A value proposition is “a clear statement of the concrete results a customer will get from purchasing and using your products and/or services. … It is focused on outcomes. Your value proposition statement details the value you provide in an easy-to-remember synopsis that your
client can easily grasp and remember… your value proposition … should relieve their pain … ”
Value propositions are not explicitly documented in a Business Scenario; however, the importance of understanding a customer’s Business Scenario to a solutions provider cannot be understated.

A Business Scenario is developed over a number of phases that formulate, verify, and refine a premise of the business requirements driving an effort. Each phase is comprised of steps to plan the phase, gather information, analyze information gathered, document the results, and review the results of the Business Scenario, as depicted in Figure 3-2.

In each phase, each of the elements of a Business Scenario (listed above) is successively improved. The refinement phase involves deciding whether to consider the scenario complete and go to the next phase of the TOGAF Architecture Development Method (ADM) [C220], or whether further refinement is necessary. This is accomplished by asking whether the current state of the Business Scenario is fit for the purpose of carrying requirements downstream in the architecture process.
The three phases of developing a Business Scenario and steps are described in detail in Figure 3-2 and Section 3.2.
Figure 3-2: Phases and Steps of Developing a Business Scenario

可采用多种技术：信息研究、定性分析、定量分析、问卷、信息请求等。在面对面工作坊之前，应尽可能“离线”收集并预处理信息。例如，信息请求可包括索取战略与运营计划；此类文档通常极具洞察力，但所含信息通常需要大量预处理。若可能，可用这些信息在工作坊前生成业务场景初稿，以增进架构师的理解与信心，并提升工作坊对参与者的价值。

收集信息的一个非常有用的方式是举办**业务场景工作坊**：由业务场景顾问引导一小群精选的业务代表回答一系列问题，以引出与架构工作所处理问题相关的信息。与会者必须从组织业务与技术高层中精心挑选，重要的是能且愿意坦诚开放地提供信息。若已有业务场景草案（例如通过本步骤预处理信息形成），工作坊也可用于评审草案状态。

有时需要多次工作坊：有时把业务侧信息收集与技术侧分开，有时只是为了从更多人处获得更多信息。

收集信息时，架构师可通过获取“真实世界案例”大大增强业务场景；引用真实案例时，应注意保持相关方匿名，避免指责。

收集步骤可考虑的活动包括：

- 拟定应回答的问题；
- 收集公开可用数据或开展早期问卷；
- 预处理公开数据（注意耗时）；
- 基于公开数据形成关键要素的“稻草人”理解；
- 针对缺口更新问题；
- 准备引导收集机制的全部材料；
- 实施所选信息收集机制；
- 举办一次或多次工作坊（若选择工作坊方式）：
  - 就问题主题与范围取得利益相关者总体一致；
  - 从利益相关者中取得支持者，并请其提供代表名单；
  - 工作坊前向受邀者发送邀请与问题；
  - 确定引导者与记录员；
  - 制定议程；
  - 制作工作坊材料（含“稻草人”业务场景）；
  - 布置场地（白板纸、U 形桌、白板、会议接入等）；
  - 举办工作坊并以电子方式记录全部信息。

source_units.text_en: 3.2.2. Gathering Step

The Gathering step is where information is collected on each of the areas in Figure 3-1. The objective is to obtain valid data to shape, confirm, and/or deny the premise driving the effort. If information gathering procedures and practices are already in place in an organization – for example, to gather information for strategic planning – they should be used as appropriate, either during Business Scenario workshops or in place of Business Scenario workshops.

Multiple techniques may be used in this step, such as information research, qualitative analysis, quantitative analysis, surveys, requests for information, etc. As much information as possible should be gathered and preprocessed “off-line” prior to any face-to-face workshops (described below). For example, a request for information may include a request for strategic and operational plans. Such documents typically provide great insights, but the information that they contain usually requires significant preprocessing. The information may be used to generate an initial draft of the Business Scenario prior to the workshop, if possible. This will increase the understanding and confidence of the architect, and the value of the workshop to its participants.

A very useful way to gather information is to hold Business Scenario workshops, whereby a Business Scenario consultant leads a select and small group of business representatives through a number of questions to elicit the information surrounding the problem being addressed by the architecture effort. The workshop attendees must be carefully selected from high levels in the business and technical sides of the organization. It is important to get people that can and will provide information openly and honestly. Where a draft of the Business Scenario already exists – for example, as a result of preprocessing information gathered during this step, as described above – the workshop may also be used to review the state of the Business Scenario draft.

Sometimes it is necessary to have multiple workshops: in some cases, to separate the gathering of information on the business side from the gathering of information on the technical side; and in other cases simply to get more information from more people.

When gathering information, the architect can greatly strengthen the Business Scenario by obtaining “real-world examples”; i.e., case studies to which the reader can easily relate. When citing real-world examples, it is important to maintain a level of anonymity of the parties involved, to avoid blame.
Activities to consider in the Gathering step include:
• Create questions you believe should be answered
• Gather data that is openly available or employ early surveys
• Preprocess openly available data – note this is time-consuming
• Develop a strawman “understanding” of the key elements based on open data
• Update questions for gaps
• Prepare all material to guide the gather mechanism
• Implement chosen information gathering mechanism
• Hold one or more workshops (if chosen method is a workshop)
◦Get general agreement from stakeholders on the subject and scope of the problem
◦Get champions from stakeholders and get them to supply names of representatives
◦Send invitations and questions to invitees prior to workshop
◦Obtain a facilitator and recorder
◦Create an agenda
◦Create workshop materials – including a “strawman” Business Scenario
◦Prepare room with flip charts, U-shape table, white board, conference hook-up as appropriate
◦Hold the workshop and capture all information from the workshop electronically

分析步骤是真正开展大量业务架构工作之处，目标是形成业务场景关键要素的统一视图：处理并记录所收集信息，并创建（通常为可视化的）模型来表现信息。

分析步骤利用业务场景顾问的知识与经验，借助过往工作形成描绘所捕获信息所需的模型。注意：产出的模型与文档未必逐字复述访谈内容，而是按真实底层需求进行过滤与转译。

分析步骤中重要的是保持业务场景关键要素之间的联系。一种有助于保持联系的技术是创建矩阵，把业务流程与以下各项关联：

- 利益相关方群体；
- 人的参与者；
- 计算机参与者；
- 问题；
- 目标。

如此，业务流程成为绑定焦点——这在多数情况下很合理，因为所追求的通常是业务流程改进。

分析步骤可考虑的活动包括：

- 把所有原始数据集中一处并锁定为只读；
- 为每个关键要素建立单独电子表格收集相关数据；
- 把原始数据复制到相应电子表格的原始数据列；
- 对文本数据进行迭代转换与归一化（语义处理）：
  - 把复合陈述拆为单点；
  - 通过亲和分析、综合与抽象，把原始数据转换为归一化清单；
  - 进一步亲和分析，为清单创建类别；
  - 记录每一步转换；
- 对可计算数据建立汇总机制——进行计算；
- 新建电子表格，建立关联全部关键要素的矩阵；
- 开展业务与能力分析，生成一组业务与技术需求；
- 对每个关键要素的答案评估完整性与正确性；
- 酌情为所收集的数据起草模型。

source_units.text_en: 3.2.3. Analyzing Step

The Analyzing step is where a great deal of real Business Architecture work is actually done. The objective of this step is to develop a uniform view of the key elements of a Business Scenario. This is where the information that is gathered is processed and documented, and where the models are created to represent that information, typically visually.

The Analyzing step takes advantage of the knowledge and experience of the Business Scenario consultant using past work and experience to develop the models necessary to depict the information captured. Note that the models and documentation produced are not necessarily reproduced verbatim from interviews, but rather filtered and translated according to the real underlying needs.

In the Analyzing step it is important to maintain linkages between the key elements of the Business Scenario. One technique that assists in maintaining such linkages is the creation of matrices that are used to relate business processes to each of:
• Constituencies
• Human Actors
• Computer Actors
• Issues
• Objectives
In this way, the business process becomes the binding focal point, which makes a great deal of sense, since in most cases it is business process improvement that is being sought.
Activities to be considered in the Analyzing step include:
• Collect all raw data in one place and lock it as read-only
• Create a separate spreadsheet to collect all relevant data per key element
• Copy raw data into a raw data column(s) of the appropriate spreadsheet per key element
• Textual data collected must iteratively transform and normalize raw data – semantics!
◦Break compounds into single points
◦Using affinity analysis, synthesis, and abstraction transform raw data into a normalized list
◦Using further affinity analysis create categories for the list
◦Each transformation step should be recorded in spreadsheet
• For calculable data:
◦Build the mechanisms to aggregate the data as findings – do the math!
• Create a new spreadsheet to build a matrix linking all the key elements
• Perform business and capability analysis to generate a set of business and technical requirements
• For each of the key elements assess answers for completeness and correctness
• Draft models of data collected as appropriate

source_units.text_en: 3.2.5. Reviewing Step

The Reviewing step is where the results are fed back to the sponsors of the project to ensure that there is a shared understanding of the full scope of the problem, and the potential depth of the technical impact. The goal is to get buy-in or stop.

Multiple Business Scenario workshops or “readout” meetings with the sponsors and involved parties are recommended. The meetings should be set up to be open and interactive. It is recommended to have exercises built into meeting agendas, in order to test attendees’ understanding and interest levels, as well as to test the architect’s own assumptions and results.
This step is extremely important, as the absence of shared expectations is in many cases the root cause of project failures.
Activities that should be considered in this step include:
• Vet the models and documentation
• Consider readout sessions
• Capture results
• Update document and models
• Identify internal and external reviewers by name
• Allocate specific sections to specific reviewers
• Craft review guidelines
• Send notification to reviewers
• Conduct a formal review of content
• Final update document and models
• Poll the stakeholders on moving forward based on the document

source_units.text_en: 3.3. Phases

The steps above are repeated in the following phases that go from creating a premise to having a Business Scenario that has been approved by the leaders of the business. This Business Scenario document is then placed in the Requirements Repository as the high-level requirements statement that drives the architecture work downstream and is used to validate the quality of the architecture.

sections.translation_zh: 每项工作都始于某种问题概念及处理该问题的方法。例如，企业可能有系统割裂、无法通信的问题，并认为可通过实施 ERP 系统解决。这一主张就是前提。该前提实质上预设了一个未明说问题的答案——ERP 真能减少我所有系统无法互操作的问题吗？有时该前提与未明说的问题未被审视，这可能是关键错误。本阶段试图理解前提及需审视的未明说问题，确保架构项目切中要害。

source_units.text_en: 3.3.1. Premise Formulation Phase

Every effort starts with some notion of a problem and an approach to dealing with a problem. For example, an enterprise might have the problem of disparate systems that do not communicate and they may have the notion that to address the problem they may implement an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. This proposition is an example of a premise. This premise in essence presumes an answer to an unstated question – do ERPs actually reduce my problem of all my systems that do not interoperate? Sometimes this premise and the unstated question do not get examined, which can be a critical mistake. In this phase we attempt to develop an understanding of the premise and unstated question or questions that need to be examined to ensure an architecture project is on point.

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 检查前提及未明说问题，避免把ERP等既定方案当作真实问题。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: ERP是说明性例子，不是本指南推荐的通用解决方案。

source_units.text_en: 4. Contents of a Business Scenario

The documentation of a Business Scenario should contain all the important details about the scenario. It should capture, and sequence, the critical steps and interactions between actors that address the situation. It should also declare all the relevant information about all actors, specifically: the different responsibilities of the actors; the key pre-conditions that have to be met prior to proper system functionality; and the technical requirements for the service to be of acceptable quality.
There are two main types of content: graphics (models) and descriptive text. Both have a part to play:

• Business Scenario models capture business and technology views in a graphical form, to aid comprehension; specifically, they relate actors and interactions, and give a starting point to confirm specific requirements

source_units.text_en: 5. Contributions to the Business Scenario

It is important to realize that the creation of a Business Scenario is not solely the province of the architect. As mentioned previously, business line management and other stakeholders in the enterprise are involved to ensure that the business goals are accurately captured. In addition, depending on the relationship that an organization has with its IT vendors, the latter also may be involved to ensure that the roles of technical solutions are also accurately captured, and to ensure communication with the vendors.

Typically, the involvement of the business management is greatest in the early stages while the business problems are being explored and captured; while the involvement of the architect is greatest in the later stages and when architectural solutions are being described. Similarly, if vendors are involved in the Business Scenario process, the involvement of the customer side (business management plus Enterprise Architects) is greatest in the early stages, while that of the vendors is greatest in the later stages when the role of specific technical solutions is being explored and captured. This concept is illustrated in Figure 5-1.
Figure 5-1: Relative Contributions to a Business Scenario

Vendor IT architects might be able to assist enterprise IT architects with integration of the vendor’s products into the Enterprise Architecture. This assistance most probably falls in the middle of the timeline in Figure 5-1.

source_units.text_en: 6. Business Scenarios and the TOGAF ADM

Business Scenarios figure most prominently in the initial phase of the TOGAF ADM cycle, Phase A: Architecture Vision [C220], when they are used to define relevant business requirements, and to build consensus with business management and other stakeholders. They are also used in the Business Architecture phase to derive the characteristics of the architecture directly from the high-level requirements of the business.
The business requirements are referred to throughout all phases of an ADM lifecycle; see Figure 6-1.
Figure 6-1: Relevance of Requirements throughout the TOGAF ADM

Business Scenarios can also be used in any ADM phase, if there is a need to derive requirements. For example, they can be used in the Preliminary Phase to define requirements for establishing an Enterprise Architecture capability.

Because business requirements are important throughout all phases of the ADM cycle, the Business Scenario technique has an important role to play in the TOGAF ADM, by ensuring that the business requirements themselves are complete and correct.

source_units.text_en: 7. Developing Business Scenarios

sections.translation_zh:
利益相关者（如业务管理者、最终用户）会告诉你他们想要什么，但作为架构师，你仍必须自行理解业务，因此必须了解系统中最重要的参与者。如果利益相关者并不清楚自己想要什么：

- 花时间观察并记录他们今天的工作方式；
- 以日后可用的方式组织信息；
- 从领域专家处发掘关键业务规则；
- 始终聚焦于需要达成什么，以及如何达成。

这项工作为从业务需求到技术解决方案的推理链提供锚点。开始时勤勉、批判，日后会有回报。

source_units.text_en: 7.1. General Guidelines

The stakeholders (e.g., business managers, end users) will tell you what they want, but as an architect you must still gain an understanding of the business, so you must know the most important actors in the system. If the stakeholders do not know what they want:
• Take time, observe, and record how they are working today
• Structure information in such a way that it can be used later
• Uncover critical business rules from domain experts
• Stay focused on what needs to be accomplished, and how it is to be accomplished
This effort provides the anchor for a chain of reason from business requirements through to technical solutions. It will pay off later to be diligent and critical at the start.

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 工作坊问题需按情境选择，不存在所有情况通用的唯一问题集合。

evidence.quote_en: no single set of appropriate questions to ask in all situations

sections.title_en: 7.2.1. Identifying, Documenting, and Ranking the Problem
sections.translation_zh:
问题是否被描述为“需要完成什么”（像流程中的步骤），而非“如何做”（技术“推动”）？

如果问题过于具体或本身就是一个“如何”：

- 亮起红旗；
- 追问“为什么需要那样做？”

如果问题过于模糊或不可行动：

- 亮起红旗；
- 追问“你需要做什么，或者问题解决后你将能做什么？”

提出有助于识别问题存在于何处、何时的问题：

- 你在哪里遇到这个特定问题？在哪个业务流程中？
- 你何时遇到这些问题？流程开始、中间还是结束？

提出有助于识别问题成本的问题：

- 你是否核算了与该问题相关的成本？如果是，有哪些？
- 是否存在隐性成本？如果有，是什么？
- 该问题的成本是否被计入其他事物的成本？如果是，是哪个、多少？
- 该问题是否表现为质量不佳，或让人感觉组织未有效发挥作用？

source_units.text_en: 7.2.1. Identifying, Documenting, and Ranking the Problem
Is the problem described as a statement of what needs to be accomplished, like steps in a process, and not how (with technology “push”)?
If the problem is too specific or a “how”:
• Raise a red flag
• Ask “why do you need to do it that way?” questions
If the problem is too vague or not actionable:
• Raise a red flag
• Ask “what is it you need to do, or will be able to do if this problem is solved?” questions
Ask questions that help to identify where and when the problem exists:
• Where are you experiencing this particular problem? In what business process?
• When do you encounter these issues? During the beginning of the process, the middle, the end?
Ask questions that help to identify the costs of the problem:
• Do you account for the costs associated with this problem? If so, what are they?
• Are there hidden costs? If so, what are they?
• Is the cost of this problem covered in the cost of something else? If so, what and how much?
• Is the problem manifested in terms of poor quality or a perception of an ineffective organization?

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 问题过度技术化时追问为何，过度模糊时追问问题解决后能完成什么。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 分别识别位置、时间、直接与隐性成本，不先指定技术方案。

evidence.quote_en: If the problem is too vague or not actionable
perception of an ineffective organization

sections.title_en: 7.2.2. Identifying the Business and Technical Environment and Documenting in Models
sections.title_zh: 7.2.2 识别业务与技术环境并记录在模型中
sections.translation_zh:
关于业务环境的问题：

- 哪个关键流程受这些问题困扰？需要处理的主要步骤是什么？
- 内部业务部门的位置/规模如何？
- 外部业务伙伴的位置/规模如何？
- 是否存在与该情境相关的特定业务规则与法规？

关于当前技术环境的问题：

- 哪些技术组件已被预设与该问题相关？
- 是否存在技术约束？
- 是否有适用的技术原则？

source_units.text_en: 7.2.2. Identifying the Business and Technical Environment and Documenting in Models
Questions to ask about the business environment:
• What key process suffers from the issues? What are the major steps that need to be processed?
• What is the location/scale of internal business departments?
• What is the location/scale of external business partners?
• Are there any specific business rules and regulations related to the situation?
Questions to ask about the current technology environment:
• What technology components are already presupposed to be related to this problem?
• Are there any technology constraints?
• Are there any technology principles that apply?

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 业务环境与技术环境分别询问流程、规模、规则、约束和原则。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 已被预设相关不代表已经验证相关。

evidence.quote_en: What technology components are already presupposed

sections.translation_zh:
“做什么”是否有充分的“为什么”理由支撑？如果没有，请就以下方面索要可度量的理由：

- 投资回报；
- 可扩展性；
- 性能需求；
- 对标准的符合性；
- 易用性度量。

source_units.text_en: 7.2.3. Identifying and Documenting Objectives
Is the “what” sufficiently backed up with the rationale for “why”? If not, ask for measurable rationale in the following areas:
• Return on investment
• Scalability
• Performance needs
• Compliance to standards
• Ease-of-use measures

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 用投资回报、扩展性、性能、标准符合性和易用性等可度量理由支持目标。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 题单没有指定通用数值门槛。

evidence.quote_en: ask for measurable rationale

sections.title_en: 7.2.4. Identifying Human Actors and their Place in the Business Model
sections.title_zh: 7.2.4 识别人的参与者及其在业务模型中的位置
sections.translation_zh:
参与者（actor）代表任何与系统交互或在系统内交互的事物，可以是人、机器或计算机程序。参与者发起与系统的活动；例如：

- 计算机用户与计算机；
- 电话用户与电话；
- 工资核算员与工资系统；
- 互联网订户与 Web 浏览器。

参与者代表用户所扮演的角色；即用户是使用系统时扮演某个角色的人（例如，John（用户）是调度员（参与者））。每个参与者以不同方式使用系统（否则他们应是同一参与者）。从不同视角询问将涉及的人，例如：

- 开发人员；
- 维护人员；
- 操作人员；
- 管理员；
- 用户。

source_units.text_en: 7.2.4. Identifying Human Actors and their Place in the Business Model
An actor represents anything that interacts with or within the system. This can be a human, or a machine, or a computer program. Actors initiate activity with the system; for example:
• Computer user with the computer
• Phone user with the telephone
• Payroll clerk with the payroll system
• Internet subscriber with the web browser

An actor represents a role that a user plays; i.e., a user is someone playing a role while using the system (e.g., John (user) is a dispatcher (actor)). Each actor uses the system in different ways (otherwise they should be the same actor). Ask about the humans that will be involved, from different viewpoints, such as:
• Developer
• Maintainer
• Operator
• Administrator
• User

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 参与者表示用户在与系统交互时所扮演的角色，可以是人、机器或程序。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: John这个具体用户与dispatcher角色分开；角色并不等于组织岗位或人员实例。

evidence.quote_en: An actor represents a role that a user plays

sections.title_en: 7.2.5. Identifying Computer Actors and their Place in the Technology Model
sections.title_zh: 7.2.5 识别计算机参与者及其在技术模型中的位置
sections.translation_zh: 同样从不同视角询问可能涉及的计算机组件。它们必须做什么？

source_units.text_en: 7.2.5. Identifying Computer Actors and their Place in the Technology Model
Ask about the computer components likely to be involved, again from different points of view. What must they do?

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 从不同视角识别计算组件及其需要完成的行为。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 先描述职责，不凭组件名称猜测实现。

evidence.quote_en: What must they do?

sections.title_en: 7.2.6. Documenting Roles, Responsibilities, Measures of Success, and Required Scripts
sections.title_zh: 7.2.6 记录角色、职责、成功度量与所需脚本
sections.translation_zh:
定义角色时，可提出如下问题：

- 该参与者的主要任务是什么？
- 该参与者是否需要读取/写入/更改任何信息？
- 该参与者是否需要把外部变化告知系统？
- 该参与者是否希望被告知意外变化？

source_units.text_en: 7.2.6. Documenting Roles, Responsibilities, Measures of Success, and Required Scripts
When defining roles, ask questions like:
• What are the main tasks of the actor?
• Will the actor have to read/write/change any information?
• Will the actor have to inform the system about outside changes?
• Does the actor wish to be informed about unexpected changes?

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 角色分析询问任务、读写修改信息、外部变化输入和意外变化通知。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 问题表达待收集事实，不能直接存成已授权访问权限。

evidence.quote_en: read/write/change any information

sections.title_en: 7.2.7. Checking for Fitness-for-Purpose and Refining, if Necessary
sections.title_zh: 7.2.7 检查适用性并在必要时细化
sections.translation_zh:
是否有足够信息识别谁/什么可以满足该需求？如果没有，进一步深入探询。

是否描述了该需求需要在何时、以何种频率得到处理？如果没有，询问时间安排。

source_units.text_en: 7.2.7. Checking for Fitness-for-Purpose and Refining, if Necessary
Is there enough information to identify who/what could fulfill the requirement? If not, probe more deeply.
Is there a description of when, and how often, the requirement needs to be addressed? If not, ask about timing.

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 适用性检查包括谁或什么能满足需求，以及处理时机和频率。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 不足时再深入和细化，不把无答案视为通过。

evidence.quote_en: when, and how often

source_units.text_en: 8. Business Scenario Documentation

sections.translation_zh:
有效的业务场景文档需要在“确保细节可获取”与“防止细节喧宾夺主、压垮读者”之间取得平衡。为此，业务场景文档应把主要发现放在正文，把细节放在附录。

在附录中：

- 捕获业务场景的全部重要细节：
  - 情境描述与理由；
  - 所有度量；
  - 所有参与者角色与子度量；
  - 所有所需服务；
- 捕获处理该情境的参与者之间的关键步骤，并对交互排序；
- 声明所有参与者的相关信息：
  - 划分参与者的职责；
  - 列出系统正常运作前必须满足的前提条件；
  - 提供服务达到可接受质量的技术要求。

在业务场景正文中：

- 对附录中的细节进行概括，提炼所有相关数据。

source_units.text_en: 8.1. Textual Documentation

Effective Business Scenario documentation requires a balance between ensuring that the detail is accessible, and preventing it from overshadowing the results and overwhelming the reader. To this end, the Business Scenario document should have the main findings in the body of the document and the details in appendices.
In the appendices:
• Capture all the important details about a Business Scenario:
◦Situation description and rationale
◦All measurements
◦All actor roles and sub-measurements
◦All services required
• Capture the critical steps between actors that address the situation, and sequence the interactions
• Declare relevant information about all actors:
◦Partition the responsibility of the actors
◦List pre-conditions that have to be met prior to proper system functionality
◦Provide technical requirements for the service to be of acceptable quality
In the main body of the Business Scenario:
• Generalize all the relevant data from the detail in the appendices

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 正文保留主要发现，附录保留细节、度量、交互及前提条件。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 正文摘要不能取代附录细节的可追溯保留。

evidence.quote_en: main findings in the body of the document and the details in appendices

sections.translation_zh:
记住使用模型的目的是：

- 帮助理解；
- 为确认需求提供起点；
- 关联参与者与交互。

保持图清晰、整洁：

- 不要在一张图中放太多内容；
- 图越简单越容易理解。

为便于引用而给图编号：

- 维护编号目录，避免重复。

source_units.text_en: 8.2. Business Scenario Models
Remember the purpose of using models is to:
• Help comprehension
• Give a starting point to confirm requirements
• Relate actors and interactions
Keep drawings clear and neat:
• Do not put too much into one diagram
• Simpler diagrams are easier to understand
Number diagrams for easy reference:
• Maintain a catalog of the numbers to avoid duplicates

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 模型用于帮助理解、确认需求及关联交互，图号需统一管理。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 简化图形应保持语义，而非删除必要约束。

evidence.quote_en: Maintain a catalog of the numbers to avoid duplicates

sections.title_zh: 9 总体目标与具体目标指南

source_units.text_en: 9. Guidelines on Goals and Objectives

sections.translation_zh:
架构开发的首批步骤之一，是定义开发的总体目标与具体目标。具体目标应源自组织的业务目标，以及 IT 被认为对达成这些目标所作贡献的方式。

每个组织在这方面的表现不同：有的把 IT 视为企业的驱动力，有的把 IT 视为支持角色，只是把已有业务流程自动化。关键在于，架构目标应与组织的业务目标与具体目标紧密对齐。

source_units.text_en: 9.1. The Importance of Goals

One of the first steps in the development of an architecture is to define the overall goals and objectives for the development. The objectives should be derived from the business goals of the organization, and the way in which IT is seen to contribute to meeting those goals.

Every organization behaves differently in this respect, some seeing IT as the driving force for the enterprise and others seeing IT in a supporting role, simply automating the business processes which already exist. The essential thing is that the architectural objectives should be very closely aligned with the business goals and objectives of the organization.

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 架构具体目标应从组织业务总体目标及IT贡献定位导出。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: IT可为驱动力或支持角色，依组织而定。

evidence.quote_en: very closely aligned with the business goals and objectives

sections.translation_zh:
目标不仅要以一般性措辞陈述，还需附加具体度量，使其如前述那样成为 SMART。

为此投入的精力将使架构演进周期的发起人获得更大的清晰度。它会在循环的每一步把拟议解决方案更紧密地引向目标，从而带来回报。对组织内不同利益相关者以及供应商和顾问而言，有一把衡量适用性的清晰标尺极为有益。若做得好，可用 ADM 把具体决策追溯到评价准则，从而给出其正当性依据。

下文目标改编自以往版本 TOGAF 标准中的目标。它们是目标的类别，每类附有一组可能的具体目标。每个具体目标都应以针对具体任务的度量与指标使其 SMART。然而，由于实际工作取决于具体的架构项目，不可能提供适用于任何项具体目标通用 SMART 具体目标清单。

因此，这里只提供一些 SMART 具体目标示例。

source_units.text_en: 9.2. The Importance of SMART Objectives
Not only must goals be stated in general terms, but also specific measures need to be attached to them to make them SMART, as described earlier.

The amount of effort spent in doing this will lead to greater clarity for the sponsors of the architecture evolution cycle. It will pay back by driving proposed solutions much more closely toward the goals at each step of the cycle. It is extremely helpful for the different stakeholders inside the organization, as well as for suppliers and consultants, to have a clear yardstick for measuring fitness-for-purpose. If done well, the ADM can be used to trace specific decisions back to criteria, and thus yield their justification.

The goals below have been adapted from those given in previous versions of the TOGAF Standard. These are categories of goals, each with a list of possible objectives. Each of these objectives should be made SMART with specific measures and metrics for the task. However, since the actual work to be done will be specific to the architecture project concerned, it is not possible to provide a list of generic SMART objectives that will relate to any project.
Instead, we provide here some example SMART objectives.

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 具体目标需按任务加度量，无法给出适用于所有项目的通用SMART目标清单。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 把决策追溯到criteria评价准则，不自动解释为技术标准。

evidence.quote_en: not possible to provide a list of generic SMART objectives

corrections.old_zh: 把具体决策追溯到标准
corrections.new_zh: 把具体决策追溯到评价准则
corrections.reason_zh: criteria是决策评价准则，不是直接等同技术标准standards。

evidence.quote_en: trace specific decisions back to criteria

sections.title_zh: 9.2.1 使具体目标符合SMART的示例
sections.translation_zh:
在下文“提高用户生产率”这一总目标标题下，有一个提供“一致的用户界面”的具体目标，其描述如下：

“一致的用户界面将确保所有用户可访问的功能与服务，无论应用或站点，都以相似、可预测的方式呈现和运行。这将带来更高的效率与更少的用户错误，进而可能降低恢复成本。”

要使该具体目标 SMART，我们依次询问它是否具体、可度量、可行动、现实、有时限，然后对该具体目标作相应补充。

以下是对该具体目标按这些标准所作的分析：

- **具体**：提供“一致的用户界面，确保所有用户可访问的功能与服务无论应用或站点都以相似、可预测的方式呈现和运行”这一具体目标相当具体；但第二句所列的度量可以更具体。
- **可度量**：如上所述，该具体目标可度量，但可以更具体；第二句可修改为（例如）：“这将使用户效率提高 10%、订单录入用户错误减少 20%，进而可能使订单录入成本降低 5%。”
- **可行动**：该具体目标看起来确实可行动；显然必须提供用户界面的一致性，而这可以由负责向用户设备提供用户界面的人来处理。
- **现实**：提供“一致的用户界面，确保所有用户可访问的功能与服务无论应用或站点都以相似、可预测的方式呈现和运行”这一具体目标可能并不现实；考虑到当今用户端使用 PDA 的情况，我们可能需要补充该具体目标，以确保下游开发人员不会不适当地设计出妨碍使用新技术的方案——该具体目标可改写为“跨越提供类似功能的用户界面设备的一致用户界面，确保……”
- **有时限**：所述具体目标没有时限；要有时限，该具体目标可改写为“到第三季度末，提供一致的用户界面……”

上述分析得出一个更接近如下的 SMART 具体目标（再次提醒，这只是示例）：

“到第三季度末，在提供类似功能的各类用户界面设备上提供一致的用户界面，确保所有用户可访问的功能与服务在使用这些设备时，无论应用或站点，都以相似、可预测的方式呈现和运行。这将使用户效率提高 10%、订单录入用户错误减少 20%，进而可能使订单录入成本降低 5%。”

> 示例边界：第三季度末、效率提高 10%、订单录入错误减少 20%、成本可能降低 5% 都是说明如何形成 SMART 具体目标的示例，未成为任何当前项目的实际基线、承诺或已达成效果。PDA 也是原文保留的历史设备示例。

source_units.text_en: 9.2.1. Example of Making Objectives SMART
Under the general goal heading “Improve User Productivity” below, there is an objective to provide a “Consistent User Interface” and it is described as follows:

“A consistent user interface will ensure that all user-accessible functions and services will appear and behave in a similar, predictable fashion regardless of application or site. This will lead to better efficiency and fewer user errors, which in turn may result in lower recovery costs.”
To make this objective SMART, we ask whether the objective is specific, measurable, actionable, realistic, and time-bound, and then augment the objective appropriately.
The following captures an analysis of these criteria for the stated objective:

• Specific: The objective of providing “a consistent user interface that will ensure all user-accessible functions and services will appear and behave in a similar, predictable fashion regardless of application or site” is pretty specific; however, the measures listed in the second sentence could be more specific

• Measurable: As stated above, the objective is measurable, but could be more specific; the second sentence could be amended to read (for example): “this will lead to 10% greater user efficiency and 20% fewer order entry user errors, which in turn may result in 5% lower order entry costs”

• Actionable: The objective does appear to be actionable; it seems clear that consistency of the user interface must be provided, and that could be handled by whoever is responsible for providing the user interface to the user device

• Realistic: The objective of providing “a consistent user interface that will ensure all user-accessible functions and services will appear and behave in a similar, predictable fashion regardless of application or site” might not be realistic; considering the use today of PDAs at the user end might lead us to augment this objective to ensure that the downstream developers don’t unduly create designs that hinder the use of new technologies – the objective could be re-stated as “a consistent user interface, across user interface devices that provide similar functionality that will ensure …”
• Time-bound: The objective as stated is not time-bound; to be time-bound the objective could be re- stated as “by the end of Q3, provide a consistent …”
The above results in a SMART objective that looks more like this (again remember this is an example):

“By the end of Q3, provide a consistent user interface across user interface devices that provide similar functionality to ensure all user-accessible functions and services appear and behave in a similar way when using those devices in a predictable fashion, regardless of application or site. This will lead to 10% greater user efficiency and 20% fewer order entry user errors, which in turn may result in 5% lower order entry costs.”

semantic_rules.statement_zh: Q3、10%、20%、5%为演示如何使界面一致性具体目标SMART的示例。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 成本降低5%保留may；需对设备功能差异限定一致性范围。

evidence.quote_en: again remember this is an example

sections.title_zh: 9.3 总体目标与具体目标的类别
sections.translation_zh:
尽管每个组织都会有自己的目标集合，一些示例可能有助于制定组织特定的清单。下文给出的是目标的类别，每类附有一组可能的具体目标，改编自以往版本 TOGAF 标准中的目标。

下文每个具体目标都应以针对相关任务的具体度量与指标使其 SMART，如上述示例所示。然而，实际工作取决于具体的架构项目，不可能提供适用于任何项具体目标通用 SMART 具体目标清单。

source_units.text_en: 9.3. Categories of Goals and Objectives

Although every organization will have its own set of goals, some examples may help in the development of an organization-specific list. The goals given below are categories of goals, each with a list of possible objectives, which have been adapted from the goals given in previous versions of the TOGAF Standard.

- **通用开发**：多个业务领域共用的应用只开发或采购一次并复用，而非由各业务领域分别开发；
- **开放系统环境**：建立基于标准的通用运行环境，可在全组织范围内接纳新标准、新技术与新应用；该基于标准的环境将为通用应用开发提供基础，并促进软件复用；

source_units.text_en: 9.3.6. Goal: Improve Effectiveness of IT Organization
IT organization effectiveness can be realized through the following objectives:
• Increased rollout of new projects
• Decreased time to roll out new projects
• Lower cost in rolling out new projects
• Decreased loss of service continuity when rolling out new projects
• Common development: applications that are common to multiple business areas will be developed or acquired once and re-used rather than separately developed by each business area

• Open systems environment: a standards-based common operating environment, which accommodates the injection of new standards, technologies, and applications on an organization- wide basis, will be established; this standards-based environment will provide the basis for development of common applications and facilitate software re-use

• Use of products: as far as possible, hardware-independent, off-the-shelf items should be used to satisfy requirements in order to reduce dependence on custom developments and to reduce development and maintenance costs

• Software re-use: for those applications that must be custom developed, development of portable applications will reduce the amount of software developed and add to the inventory of software suitable for re-use by other systems

• Resource sharing: data processing resources (hardware, software, and data) will be shared by all users requiring the services of those resources – resource sharing will be accomplished in the context of security and operational considerations

• Integrated applications: applications available to the user will behave in a logically consistent manner across user environments, which will lead to the same benefits as a consistent user interface
• Data sharing: databases will be shared across the organization in the context of security and operational considerations, leading to increased ease-of-access to required data

sections.title_zh: 9.3.11 目标：降低生命周期成本
sections.translation_zh:
生命周期成本可通过上述多数具体目标降低。此外，以下具体目标直接针对生命周期成本的降低：

- **减少重复**：以互联开放系统取代孤立系统与自动化孤岛，将减少重叠功能、数据重复与不必要的冗余，因为开放系统可以共享数据与其他资源；
- **降低软件维护成本**：减少组织所用软件的数量与种类，将降低软件维护的工作量与成本——使用标准现成软件将进一步降低成本，因为此类软件的供应商把产品维护成本分摊到更大的用户群；
- **增量替换**：共享基础设施组件的通用接口允许分阶段替换或升级，而对运营的干扰最小；
- **降低培训成本**：通用系统与一致的人机接口（HCI）将降低培训成本。

source_units.text_en: 9.3.11. Goal: Reduce Lifecycle Costs
Lifecycle costs can be reduced through most of the objectives discussed above. In addition, the following objectives directly address reduction of lifecycle costs:

• Reduced duplication: replacement of isolated systems and islands of automation with interconnected open systems will lead to reductions in overlapping functionality, data duplication, and unneeded redundancy because open systems can share data and other resources

• Reduced software maintenance costs: reductions in the quantity and variety of software used in the organization will lead to reductions in the amount and cost of software maintenance – use of standard off-the-shelf software will lead to further reductions in costs since vendors of such software distribute their product maintenance costs across a much larger user base
• Incremental replacement: common interfaces to shared infrastructure components allow for phased replacement or upgrade with minimal operational disturbance
• Reduced training costs: common systems and consistent Human Computer Interfaces (HCIs) will lead to reduced training costs

sections.translation_zh:
组织信息的安全性可通过以下具体目标提高：

- **一致的应用安全接口**：一致的安全接口与程序将减少开发应用时的错误并提高应用可移植性；并非所有应用都需要同一套安全特性，但所使用的任何特性都应在各应用间保持一致；
- **一致的用户安全接口**：安全特性的通用用户界面将减少在系统间切换时的学习时间；
- **安全独立性**：如果架构具有良好的分层，应用部署可以使用适合特定环境的安全策略与机制；
- 与安全问题相关的服务台呼叫减少 25%；
- 网络中检测到的“误报”减少 20%（误报是指看似可采取行动的安全事件、但实际上是虚惊一场的事件）。

> 示例边界：25% 与 20% 是本节列出的可能具体目标，尚需按项目确定基线、统计口径、时限与责任；并非全行业最低门槛或当前项目结果。

source_units.text_en: 9.3.12. Goal: Improve Security
Security can be improved in the organization’s information through the following objectives:

• Consistent security interfaces for applications: consistent security interfaces and procedures will lead to fewer errors when developing applications and increased application portability; not all applications will need the same suite of security features, but any features used will be consistent across applications
• Consistent security interfaces for users: a common user interface to security features will lead to reduced learning time when moving from system to system
• Security independence: application deployment can use the security policy and mechanisms appropriate to the particular environment if there is good layering in the architecture
• A 25% reduction in calls to the help desk relating to security issues
• A 20% reduction in “false positives” detected in the network (a false positive is an event that appears to be an actionable security event, but in fact is a false alarm)

sections.translation_zh:
开发业务场景需要填补多个角色。有些角色可由同一人担任，因此角色数量之和并不意味着需要那么多人。人员配置应在规划步骤中完成：

- **项目经理**（Project Manager）：规划、执行并监控项目，使业务场景在规定时间与预算内形成文档并经过评审；
- **业务场景顾问**（Business Scenario Consultant）：引导项目朝正确方向推进，以产出高质量的业务场景；
- **业务场景分析师**（Business Scenario Analyst）：运用数据收集与分析技术，形成对业务场景各要素的共识视图；
- **业务场景作者**（Business Scenario Author）：对业务场景作出忠实、客观的叙述性描述；
- **业务场景编辑**（Business Scenario Editor）：把草稿加工成配得上 The Open Group 品牌标识的高质量可发布文档；
- **业务场景引导者**（Business Scenario Facilitator）：主持编排良好的会议与工作坊，使与会者满意且有所收获；
- **领域专家贡献者**（SME Contributors）：就拟议前提相关的特定主题提供专家建议与内容；
- **领域专家评审者**（SME Reviewers）：评审业务场景文档并提出客观、建设性的建议；
- **东道主**（Host）：为参与者提供受欢迎的环境，体现该项工作的推动力，让与会者放心开放；
- **发起人**（Sponsor）：代表高管层“买方”，说明推进该项工作的重要性，让与会者放心其将支持这项工作及后续跟进；
- **工作坊主问者与次问者**（Workshop Primary and Secondary Questioner）：提出有计划的探询性问题与追问，引出与主题相关的信息；
- **工作坊记录员**（Workshop Recorders）：忠实记录工作坊与会议的问题答案与笔记。

source_units.text_en: 10. Roles

In order to develop a Business Scenario, there are multiple roles that need to be filled. There are roles that can be filled by the same person, so the sum of the roles means you may not need that many people. Configuring the people to perform the roles is something that should be done in the Planning step:
• Project Manager: plan, execute, and monitor a project that results in a documented and vetted Business Scenario in time and on budget
• Business Scenario Consultant: guide the project so that it is moving in the right direction to result in a quality Business Scenario
• Business Scenario Analyst: apply data gathering and analysis techniques that result in consensus views of the elements of a Business Scenario
• Business Scenario Author: produce a faithful and objective narrative description of the Business Scenario
• Business Scenario Editor: take a draft and produce a high-quality publishable document deserving of The Open Group brand identity
• Business Scenario Facilitator: conduct well-orchestrated meetings and workshops that result in satisfied and fulfilled attendees
• SME Contributors: provide expert advice and content in a specific subject germane to the propose premise
• SME Reviewers: review and provide objective and constructive recommendations pertaining to the Business Scenario document
• Host: provide the welcome environment for participants that represents the impetus for the effort to reassure attendees to be open
• Sponsor: represent the executive-level “buy side” of the importance of moving forward with the effort to reassure attendees that they will support the effort and its follow-up
• Workshop Primary and Secondary Questioner: ask probing planned and follow-up questions that pull out information germane to the subject
• Workshop Recorders: faithfully capture the answers to questions and notes of workshops and meetings

semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 12项角色描述不等于必须12个人或固定编制。

sections.translation_zh:
以下提示与技巧可用于工作坊与分析中的各种情境：

- 使用真实案例；
- 用练习解决真实且相关的问题；
- 使用圆桌讨论，并确保征求每个人的意见；
- 使用主动倾听与反思性倾听；
- 在会议中使用头脑风暴与亲和分析；
- 使用“介绍你的邻座”技巧；
- 使用“我们相信”练习；
- 使用金钱或“点数”投票进行优先级排序；
- 考虑使用多轮投票和/或排序；
- 考虑使用角色扮演；
- 考虑使用备选方案分析与决策矩阵；
- 对照检查清单。

source_units.text_en: 12. Techniques and Tips
The following tips and techniques can be used in various situations during workshops and analysis:
• Use real-world examples
• Use exercises to solve a real and relevant issue
• Use roundtables and ensure you solicit everyone’s views
• Use active and reflective listening
• Use brainstorming with affinity analysis in meetings
• Use “introduce your neighbor” technique
• Use “we believe” exercise
• Use money or “credits” voting for prioritization
• Consider using multi-voting and/or rank ordering
• Consider using role play
• Consider using alternative analysis with a decision matrix
• Check the checklist

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 工作坊技巧按情境选用，部分以consider说明可考虑。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 不是每轮必须开展全部12项。

evidence.quote_en: can be used in various situations

sections.title_zh: 12.1 关于主动倾听与反思性倾听
sections.translation_zh:
- 当你希望确保某人被听到——不仅被你，而是被所有人听到时使用。
- 主动倾听（据 Wikipedia®）：
  - 一种用于咨询、培训与冲突解决的沟通技巧，要求倾听者把听到的内容反馈给说话者，即用自己的话重述或复述所听内容，以确认听到的内容，并进一步确认双方的理解。
- 反思性倾听（据 Wikipedia）：
  - 一种包含两个关键步骤的沟通策略：先设法理解说话者的想法，再把该想法回馈给说话者，以确认已正确理解；它试图“重构客户的所思所感，并转达这种理解”。

source_units.text_en: 12.1. On Active and Reflective Listening
• Use whenever you want to ensure that someone is being heard – not just by you, but by everyone
• Active listening from Wikipedia®:
◦A communication technique used in counseling, training, and conflict resolution, which

requires the listener to feed back what they hear to the speaker, by way of re-stating or paraphrasing what they have heard in their own words, to confirm what they have heard and, moreover, to confirm the understanding of both parties
• Reflective listening from Wikipedia:
◦A communication strategy involving two key steps: seeking to understand a speaker’s idea, then
offering the idea back to the speaker, to confirm the idea has been understood correctly; it attempts to “reconstruct what the client is thinking and feeling and to relay this understanding”

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 主动和反思性倾听把理解回馈给说话者确认。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 复述需获得确认，不能只凭听者觉得清楚认定共识。

evidence.quote_en: confirm the understanding of both parties

sections.title_zh: 12.2 关于头脑风暴与亲和分析
sections.translation_zh:
- 当你希望让整个团队提出想法时使用。
- 头脑风暴：
  - 一种收集所有参与者想法的结构化技术——它不是自由放任的混战；
  - 描述练习主题；
  - 说明头脑风暴规则；
  - 请每个人写下自己对主题的想法（设定一些限制，如“用一句话”）；
  - 以圆桌方式逐一获取每位参与者的想法，并记录在便利贴上；
  - 张贴便利贴；
  - 对想法进行亲和分析。
- 亲和分析：
  - 一种识别并归组相似或相关想法的手段；
  - 有助于把许多想法忠实合并为可管理的清单。

source_units.text_en: 12.2. On Brainstorming and Affinity Analysis
• Use when you want to engage the entire team to put out ideas
• Brainstorming:
◦A structured technique to gather all participant ideas – it is not a free-for-all
◦Describe the exercise subject
◦Describe rules for brainstorming
◦Ask everyone to jot down their thoughts on the subject (set some limit like “in one sentence”)
◦Proceed to get each participant’s ideas one at a time and record on sticky notes in a roundtable
manner
◦Post sticky notes
◦Do affinity analysis on ideas
• Affinity analysis:
◦A means to identify and group similar or related ideas
◦Useful to faithfully combine many ideas into a manageable list

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 头脑风暴是有结构的全员想法收集，再用亲和分析归组。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 合并想法应忠实保留观点，避免把少数意见删除成伪共识。

evidence.quote_en: it is not a free-for-all

sections.translation_zh:
- 当你需要从彼此不太了解的群体中建立团队时使用。
- 两人配对，例如 Al 和 Betty。
- 让他们交谈几分钟并互相介绍：
  - 最多五分钟；
  - 请他们聊姓名、居住地、业务、爱好等。
- 然后绕房间一周，让他们互相介绍：
  - Al 介绍 Betty，Betty 介绍 Al；
  - 让所有参与者都被介绍；
  - 若参与者为奇数，由引导者配对。

source_units.text_en: 12.3. Introduce your Neighbor
• Use when you want to build a team from a group that doesn’t know each other well
• Pair people up; e.g., Al and Betty
• Have them chat and introduce each other for a few minutes:
◦Limit to five minutes maximum
◦Ask them to chat about name, where they live, business, hobbies, etc.
• Then go around the room and have them introduce each other:
◦Al introduces Betty and Betty introduces Al
◦Have all participants introduced
◦Have facilitator pair up if there is an odd number of participants

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 陌生团队可配对互相介绍，谈话最多五分钟，奇数时引导者加入。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 这个时间限制仅属于该练习。

evidence.quote_en: Limit to five minutes maximum

sections.translation_zh:
- 当团队无法收敛，或争论方式缺乏建设性时使用。
- 退后一步，回到最初的前提。
- 问“我们相信这一点吗？”
  - 如果不信，那么“我们相信什么”？
- 维护一份“我们相信”清单。
- 将清单限制在重要信念上。
- 这些“我们相信”可以成为原则，或导向原则。

source_units.text_en: 12.4. We Believe
• Use when the team is not converging or they are arguing in a non-constructive way
• Take a step back and go to the original premise
• Ask “do we believe in this?”
◦If not what do “we believe in”?
• Maintain a list of “we believes”
• Limit the list to important beliefs
• These “we believes” could become or lead to principles

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 不收敛时退回前提整理共同信念，这些信念可能导向原则。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 共同信念不自动获得正式架构原则批准。

evidence.quote_en: could become or lead to principles

sections.title_en: 12.5. On Money or Credit Voting Prioritization
sections.title_zh: 12.5 金钱或点数投票优先级排序
sections.translation_zh:
- 当你想了解人们真正愿意把资源投入何处时使用。
- 使用假钱或“点数”。
- 给每人一个预算：
  - 不能超预算花费；
  - 可投给一项或多项；
  - 如有其他规则，应事先宣布。
- 请参与者把预算分配到一份清单上：
  - 可匿名进行（首选）；
  - 使其真实：请每个人准备好为自己的分配辩护，就像向老板辩护一样。
- 汇总预算。
- 公布结果并讨论。

source_units.text_en: 12.5. On Money or Credit Voting Prioritization
• Use when you want to get a sense of what people will really put their resources into
• Use fake money or “credits”
• Give each person a budget:
◦Can’t spend over the budget
◦Can apply to one item, or more
◦If you have other rules then announce them
• Ask participants to allocate their budget against a list:
◦Can do anonymously (preferred)
◦Make it real by asking everyone to be prepared to defend their allocation as if defending it to
their boss
• Tally the budgets
• Expose the results and discuss

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 用假钱或点数在预算内分配以识别资源优先选择，推荐匿名。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 投票不是实际付款、授信、预算批准或财务承诺。

evidence.quote_en: Use fake money or “credits”

corrections.reason_zh: credits是供练习分配的虚拟点数，避免与金融授信混淆。

evidence.quote_en: Use fake money or “credits”

sections.title_en: 12.6. On Multi-Voting and Rank Ordering Prioritization
sections.title_zh: 12.6 关于多轮投票与排序优先级
sections.translation_zh:
- 当你希望就清单事项的优先级达成共识时使用。
- 多轮投票：
  - 一种结构化制度，分步投票，每一步都缩减清单，最终缩至三到五项。
- 排序：
  - 将清单事项按 1 到 n 排序，所有排序的平均值形成集体视图。

source_units.text_en: 12.6. On Multi-Voting and Rank Ordering Prioritization
• Use whenever you want to get to a consensus view on the priority of items in a list
• Multi-voting:
◦Structured system where votes are taken in successive steps where each step reduces a list
ultimately to three to five items
• Rank ordering:
◦Where items on a list are ranked 1 to n and the average of all the ranking produces a collective
view

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 多轮投票收敛至三到五项；排序对各参与者的1到n排序取平均。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 多轮投票和排序是不同方法，不把平均排名称为因果价值评分。

evidence.quote_en: average of all the ranking produces a collective

sections.translation_zh:
- 当你希望拓展人们的视角，尤其是考虑另一种视角时使用：
  - 若你想让两个人或两个群体思考另一个人或另一个群体的观点，通常很有用。
- 描述一个情境，并把两种观点摆上桌面。
- 请个人或小组扮演该情境中的特定角色，并描述其观点与关注点：
  - 让供应商处在买方位置；
  - 让买方处在供应商位置；
  - 让患者扮演医生；
  - 让医生扮演患者。

source_units.text_en: 12.7. On Role Play
• Use when you want to expand people’s perspectives and especially consider another perspective:
◦Often useful if you want two people or two groups to think about another person’s or another
groups views
• Describe a situation and put two viewpoints on the table
• Ask a person or a group to take a specific role within that situation and describe their views and concerns:
◦Put a supplier in the situation of a buyer
◦Put a buyer in the situation of a supplier
◦Put a patient in the role of a doctor
◦Put a doctor in the role of a patient

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 角色扮演要求参与者从另一视角陈述观点和关注点。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 扮演者观点不是被代表真实利益相关者的已确认事实。

evidence.quote_en: describe their views and concerns

corrections.old_zh: 直接从情境描述跳到换位例子

sections.title_zh: 12.8 关于备选方案分析与决策矩阵
sections.translation_zh:
- 当桌上的方案太少，或看起来可能对某个既定方案有偏向时使用。
- 对备选方案进行头脑风暴，形成归一化清单。
- 把清单事项放入矩阵，并增加以下列：
  - 成本
  - 所需资源
  - 对问题的贡献
  - 可行性
  - 计算排序
- 请人们为每个单元格打分，1（最差）到 5（最佳）。
- 必要时加权重并计算。

| 备选方案 | 成本（权重=1） | 资源（权重=1） | 贡献（权重=1） | 可行性（权重=1） | 计算排序 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 方案 1 | | | | | |
| 方案 2 … | | | | | |

> 数据边界：表内 Alt 1、Alt 2 是空白模板行，没有原始评分或已计算排名。1 表示最差，5 表示最佳；成本列得分应表达相对评价，不能直接把货币成本值代入同一量表。原文只说必要时加权计算，未规定唯一评分公式或自动批准规则。

source_units.text_en: 12.8. On Alternative Analysis and Decision Matrix
• Use when there are too few approaches on the table, maybe looking as if there may be bias towards a given approach
• Brainstorm alternatives and put in a normalized list
• Put list items in a matrix with additional columns for:
◦Cost
◦Required resources
◦Contribution to problem
◦Feasibility
◦Calculated Rank
• Ask people to rank each cell 1 (worse) to 5 (best)
• Add weight if necessary and calculate

| Alternative | Cost
(weight =1) | Resources
(weight =1) | Contribution
(weight =1) | Feasibility
(weight =1) | Calculated Rank | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Alt 1 | | | | | | | Alt 2 … | | | | | |

sections.translation_zh:
业务场景有助于解决高管面临的一个最常见问题：使重大转型（例如由 IT 变革支撑的转型）与业务对齐。

任何重大项目的成功，都以它与业务需求的关联程度、以及它能否可证明地支持并使能企业达成业务成果来衡量。业务场景方法是一项重要技术，可用于定义企业架构的多个阶段，或支持任何其他重大项目，以直接从业务的高层需求推导架构特征。业务场景用于帮助识别并理解业务需求，从而导出架构开发乃至最终解决方案必须处理的业务需求。

然而，重要的是记住：**业务场景只是工具，不是目的**。它们是更大范围的架构与下游开发过程的一部分，并为该过程提供使能。架构师应使用它们，但不应迷失其中。关键是保持聚焦——警惕“功能蔓延”（feature creep），处理那些往往能带来最大价值的最重要问题。

source_units.text_en: 13. Summary
Business Scenarios help to address one of the most common issues facing executives: aligning significant transformation, such as those supported by IT changes, with the business.

The success of any major project is measured by the extent to which it is linked to business requirements, and demonstrably supports and enables the enterprise to achieve its business outcomes. The Business Scenario method is an important technique that may be used at various stages of defining an Enterprise Architecture, or in support of any other major project, to derive the characteristics of the architecture directly from the high-level requirements of the business. Business Scenarios are used to help identify and understand business needs, and thereby to derive the business requirements that the architecture development, and ultimately the solution, has to address.

However, it is important to remember that Business Scenarios are just a tool, not the objective. They are a part of, and enable, the larger process of architecture and downstream development. The architect should use them, but not get lost in them. The key is to stay focused – watch out for “feature creep”, and address the most important issues that tend to return the greatest value.
